correctness.rationale: The vertex [0:0:0:1] of the weighted ambient space is off F=0. On each weight-one affine chart, the usual hypersurface Jacobian test is equivalent to vanishing of all four homogeneous partials: the partial for the fixed coordinate follows from weighted Euler, xF_x+yF_y+zF_z=0 in characteristic 2. F_w=x²+yz; F_x=λyz(y+z). With λ nonzero, their common base-point locus is precisely [0:1:0], [0:0:1], [1:1:1]. Substituting in the two remaining partials forces w=b, d, λ+b+d respectively. Substitution into F gives b²+a, d²+e, λ²+b²+d²+a+b+c+d+e. This both exhausts the geometric singularity candidates and gives their exact existence conditions. The two characteristic-two examples meet the displayed polynomial family's λ/root restrictions and have printed inequality values (1,1,1) and (0,1,1) respectively when the disputed condition is listed first; the first is singular at the stated point, the second smooth by exhaustion.
residual_risks: The finite replay is only corroboration; the affine-chart and three-point exhaustion prove the claim over algebraically closed characteristic-two fields. Other normal forms and later tables are not audited here.

value.rationale: Although obtained by elementary differentiation, this is an actionable correction to a published classification: the printed locus includes a singular equation and excludes a smooth one in the displayed parameter coordinates. Anyone selecting or enumerating smooth members of that family needs the exact locus. The contribution is the corrected locus and separators, not a new smoothness method or an audit of downstream automorphism cases.
